## Summary

Bailon's **Visual Explainer** Claude skill just crossed **10,000 GitHub stars**. Origin story in his words: a February hunch that **agents should plan in HTML instead of markdown**. The quoted tweet is the experience claim: once you've planned with the Visual Explainer, "I can't go back to markdown plans." The skill itself (repo behind the t.co link, not resolved at capture) turns plans into visual/interactive HTML artifacts instead of markdown documents.

## Why it matters

- **The planning-representation debate, now with adoption evidence.** [[2026-09-06-phelps-agentic-planning-loop]] covered a planning *process* (/grill-me → /council → plannotator, iterate to convergence); this is the complementary claim about planning *medium* — that the plan's representation itself (rich, visual HTML vs. flat markdown) changes plan quality and reviewability. 10k stars is a real adoption signal, not just a take.
- **Connects to our own artifacts.** Our harness already produces plans and briefs as structured documents; the claim here is that *visual* structure (diagrams, layout, progressive disclosure) beats *textual* structure for both the agent planning and the human reviewing. That's testable cheaply on our next planning artifact: same plan, both representations, judge review speed and error-finding.
- **Skill-ecosystem momentum keeps compounding.** Third heavily-starred agent-skill artifact captured this quarter (with the Jev plugin cluster and the OpenClaw skills) — the ecosystem is consolidating on small, composable SKILL.md-style artifacts as the unit of agent capability. Worth tracking which of these earn a slot in our own stack.
- **Skepticism gates:** repo not opened at capture (t.co unresolved — 10k stars is self-reported in-tweet; the repo id, README, and what the skill actually outputs are unverified); the quoted "POV" is the author's own experience, n=1; star counts measure attention, not correctness; the video demo wasn't viewed.
